newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt prices ease back but seen supported.
newsitem.headline: German debt prices ease back but seen supported.

text.p: German Bunds and futures slipped swiftly into negative ground on Friday, giving back some on the gains made in a spirited previous session.
Traders said the failure of the September DTB Bund future to take on key resistance at the 103.00 level on Thursday meant that a slight setback in early dealings was on the cards.
But they said the contract should find good nearby support.
At 0715 GMT, the September Bund futures contract was 11 basis points lower on the day at 102.73, having been up to 102.86 just after the open.
"It's looking a bit weaker here this morning," said one trader at a Frankfurt-based bank. "But I don't see it falling too far. Buyers are keen to get in at lower levels."
Analysts said the main focus for the market would be the Ifo business sentiment index for June, expected to be released at 0800 GMT.
The west German index, which rose to 95.3 in May from 94.7 in April, was again expected to rise, but only to around 95.7.
"There are rumours of a stronger number, but it shouldn't do too much harm to the market because it will help the mark," the trader said.
The mark, which has been struggling in the past few sessions to hold above its lowest levels for almost six years, was trading at 1.7926/36 by 0724 GMT.
In the cash Bund market, the 10-year benchmark was quoted at 103.16, offering a bid yield of 5.569 percent.
The 10-year yield spread to Treasuries stood at 75 basis points out from around 72 basis points at Thursday's close.
